comparison: Perfect agreement on the central finding. Both evaluations find the identification of the exon-G/ABD interaction well-supported by biochemical pulldown data (C6, C10-C20). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, peer reviewers unanimously accept this as the main contribution with solid evidence.

Partial disagreement on affinity characterization (C21-C27). OpenEval finds the MST measurement and mutagenesis data SUPPORTED, while peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting that affinity measurements are insufficient and don't specifically characterize the exon-G/ABD interaction.

Complete agreement on tripartite complex and synergistic binding (C7, C28-C32). Both evaluations find the evidence SUPPORTED. Peer Reviewer 2 explicitly confirms acceptance of the independent and synergistic interaction findings.

Complete agreement on mutually exclusive binding (C9, C33-C38). Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the conclusion is inferred rather than structurally demonstrated, but peer Reviewer 2 accepts this as a key finding without critique of the pelleting assay data.

Disagreement on cellular validation rigor (C8, C39-C44). OpenEval finds the dominant-negative assay SUPPORTED with appropriate controls, while peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting insufficient controls in cellular studies despite some requested controls being added.

Agreement on exon-G deletion effects (C45-C48). Both evaluations find the data SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights the dramatic reduction in dominant-negative effect, and peer reviewers accept this as part of the modified recruitment model without specific critique.

Agreement on colocalization data (C49-C54). Both evaluations rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval finds the differential effects of exon-F versus exon-G deletion clear, and peer reviewers accept these findings as consistent with the overall model.

Agreement on speculative nature of regulatory model (C94, C98-C101, C104-C106). Both rate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes key regulatory steps are proposed but not tested; peer reviewers are more critical, with Reviewer 3 noting lack of new mechanistic data and multiple unanswered questions about regulation and function.

OpenEval evaluates background literature claims (C1-C5, C55-C82) as SUPPORTED, finding the authors accurately summarize prior work and identify the key unresolved question. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these background claims.

OpenEval finds interpretive claims about motor regulation versus binding (C83-C93) SUPPORTED by combination of current and prior data. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addressing these interpretive distinctions.
OpenEval evaluates contextual claims about structural constraints and prior literature (C95-C97, C102-C103) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these contextual claims.
